1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode. # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. # 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub. ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check |

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D low-poly FPS in Three.js with zombie wave and prop hunt modes, AK-47/RPG weapons, and ragdoll kills.

## Requirements
- 3D low-quality/low-poly shooter.
- Game modes: zombie waves and prop hunt.
- Include RPGs and AK-47s.
- Add ragdoll on kill.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) for checks and inspect only latest.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS project with vendored Three.js r180 (no framework).
- Procedural geometry, textures, and WebAudio; local bundled fonts.
- Stylized low-poly desert arena “DEAD DROP,” golden-hour lighting, industrial props.
- Two modes: endless escalating zombie waves; 95-second prop hunt with 8 mimics + 7 decoys, sonar scan on Q, decoy time penalty.
- Weapons: automatic AK-47 (30-round mag, reload) and RPG-7 (1 loaded, 6 reserve, auto reload, splash damage).
- Custom ragdoll: detaches head/torso/arms/legs into physical chunks with gravity, spin, floor bounce, blood pools.
- Touch controls and responsive HUD included.
- Static world meshes merged by material and zombie submeshes merged locally to reduce draw calls; shadow map reduced to 1024.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` full menu, HUD, pause/end screens, touch overlay.
- `styles.css` full visual design and responsive/mobile layouts.
- `src/main.js` implemented renderer, procedural map, weapons, viewmodels, enemies, waves, prop hunt, ragdolls, effects, audio, HUD, radar, controls, game loop.
- Vendored `vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/three.core.min.js`, `vendor/addons/BufferGeometryUtils.js`, licenses.
- Bundled Barlow Condensed and Space Mono fonts.
- Game loads with no JS runtime errors; zombie mode starts and spawns enemies.
- Static world merge reduced menu draw calls to ~56; gameplay with 6 enemies ~137 calls.
- Menu and gameplay screenshots captured and inspected.
- Current dev server running in tmux `deadrop` on `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Visual polish iteration: newest gameplay screenshot shows viewmodel still somewhat oversized/dark; world facade lighting improved but still fairly dark.
- Need verify prop hunt mode, ragdoll visual, explosions, pause/end screens, and mobile layout in browser.
- Need test final capture.sh flow and adaptive performance.

### Blocked
- SwiftShader software rendering only reaches ~7.5 FPS at 1024×768, limiting interactive testing; hardware performance should be higher but unverified.

## Next Move
1. Reload and test prop hunt via `DEAD_DROP.start('prop')`; screenshot and inspect prop placement, scan, and mimic/ragdoll behavior.
2. Kill an enemy (set health low or shoot) and inspect ragdoll/corpse visuals.
3. Test RPG firing/explosion and pause/end screens.
4. Inspect 390×844 mobile viewport and touch HUD/controls.
5. Tune viewmodel size/lighting and overall darkness if needed.
6. Add favicon to eliminate `/favicon.ico` 404; remove or silence stale console warnings.
7. Run `bash capture.sh` with required env (`CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR`) or verify `start.sh` flow, then commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: all game logic, rendering, effects, controls, UI wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: menu/HUD/modal DOM and importmap.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: complete UI styling and responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.module.js`: Three.js module entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.core.min.js`: required internal Three.js dependency.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/addons/BufferGeometryUtils.js`: static mesh merging.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/fonts/`: bundled display/mono fonts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest menu/gameplay JPEGs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: runtime static server entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: automated screenshot entry.

const viewScene = new THREE.Scene();
const viewCamera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(55, innerWidth/innerHeight, .01, 10);
viewScene.add(viewCamera);
const viewRoot = new THREE.Group();
viewCamera.add(viewRoot);

viewScene.add(viewHemi);
const viewFill = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd7ad, 1.2);
viewFill.position.set(.6,.8,1); viewScene.add(viewFill);
```
Then viewLight attached to viewCamera as before (child). Camera near .01.

Render:
```
renderer.render(scene,camera);
if (viewRoot.visible) { renderer.autoClear=false; renderer.clearDepth(); renderer.render(viewScene, viewCamera); renderer.autoClear=true; }
```
But we set viewRoot.visible = true when active; currently viewRoot is child of camera. We need to remove that. Move `camera.add(viewRoot)` to viewCamera. The `camera.add(viewLight)` → viewCamera.add(viewLight). Also `viewRoot.visible` toggles.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D low-poly FPS in Three.js with zombie wave and prop hunt modes, AK-47/RPG weapons, and ragdoll kills.

## Requirements
- 3D low-quality/low-poly shooter.
- Game modes: zombie waves and prop hunt.
- Include RPGs and AK-47s.
- Add ragdoll on kill.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) for checks and inspect only latest.
- Support mobile / touch layouts.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS project with vendored Three.js r180 (no framework).
- Procedural geometry, textures, WebAudio; local bundled fonts.
- Stylized low-poly desert arena “DEAD DROP,” golden-hour lighting, industrial props.
- Endless escalating zombie waves; 95-second prop hunt with 8 mimics + 7 decoys, sonar scan on Q, decoy time penalty.
- Automatic AK-47 (30-round mag, reload) and RPG-7 (1 loaded, 6 reserve, auto reload, splash damage).
- Custom ragdoll: detaches head/torso/arms/legs into physical chunks with gravity, spin, floor bounce, blood pools.
- Viewmodel rendered in a separate `viewScene`/`viewCamera` (FOV 50) composited with depth clear.
- `?touch=1` query override forces touch HUD for desktop testing.
- Static world merged by material; zombie submeshes merged locally; shadow map 1024.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` full menu, HUD, pause/end screens, touch overlay; favicon added and linked.
- `styles.css` full visual design, responsive/mobile layouts; mobile menu centering and title/lede spacing fixed.
- `src/main.js` renderer, procedural map, weapons, viewmodels, enemies, waves, prop hunt, ragdolls, effects, audio, HUD, radar, controls, game loop.
- Vendored Three.js, licenses, bundled Barlow Condensed and Space Mono fonts.
- Fixed giant dark smoke blob: particles now preserve `baseScale` instead of overwriting scale.
- Fixed critical ragdoll crash: strip circular `userData.enemy` before `Object3D.clone`.
- Fixed rocket tunneling with swept segment-sphere collision against enemies/props.
- Exposure/lighting brightened; explosion fireball reduced from giant translucent dome.
- Weapon viewmodel scale/position/pose tuned for desktop and portrait (responsive scale + x offset).
- Verified zombie mode, prop hunt, sonar scan glow/ring, mimic kill + ragdoll + blood, RPG kill/explosion, pause screen, end screen, mobile menu, mobile gameplay HUD/touch controls.
- `node --check` passes; browser console now reports 0 errors.
- Official capture runs without HTTP/JS failures, but desktop auto-start still fails actionability.

### Active
- Making the automated `capture.sh` desktop flow click `PLAY NOW` successfully in SwiftShader at 1440×900.
- Diagnosed: menu first render takes ~8–10 s; `load` at ~32 s; trial click still fails with `TimeoutError ... waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable` for ~4 s after fonts load, but succeeds after ~4–6 s more.
- Added menu idle freeze (`menuIdle`) after the first menu frame; verified `menuIdle=true`, `renderer.info.render.frame=1`, but trial click still fails immediately after fonts.
- `DEBUG=pw:actionability` produced no extra diagnostics.

### Blocked
- SwiftShader CPU rendering is extremely slow; menu rAF measured ~0.1 fps initially, ~6 fps after warm-up.
- Debug `trial click` passes only after extra settle time in standalone diagnostic; capture script clicks immediately and times out.

## Next Move
1. Determine why immediate post-fonts click is unstable despite static menu (`menuIdle=true`) and stable button rect; try delaying `document.fonts` readiness or preloading fonts, or add a lightweight always-running CSS/2D animation that keeps rAF/compositor active.
